questions.question: Wind noise while riding can:

options.text: Be easy to get used to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long exposure to wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear plugs or hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding to maintain balance.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Fit snug enough to not flap in the wind.
Be tight enough to limit your movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug enough to not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply controlled pressure to both brakes at the same time for the best quick stop. Avoid locking the brakes.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you more visible and keeps a safe distance from other vehicles.
You prefer, without regard for others.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you more visible and keeps a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you and you have space around your motorcycle. There is no single best lane position. Change your position as conditions change.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your lane position:

options.text: Has little effect on whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important for whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important for whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It also protects you from wind blasts from nearby vehicles.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle for the first time, you should:

options.text: Just start riding. Learning by doing is the best way.
Just start riding. All bikes are similar.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how they work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes to learn how they work.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Do a safety check, find all controls, and practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle stopped on the roadside with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind it.
Stop and wait until it moves.
Move to a different lane away from it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from it.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space and proceed carefully. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce speed, avoid sudden moves, and use both brakes.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Should not be a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking technique is important for safe riding.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when riding. Good ear protection lets you still hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: No matter what helmet style you choose, you get the most protection when your helmet:
questions.correctAnswerText: Fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives the best protection when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no visible damage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
Only stop to let other traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, even in warm weather.

questions.question: The risk of head or neck injury is reduced:
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding a motorcycle, no matter your speed. A quality helmet, worn properly, greatly reduces the risk of these injuries.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: The other driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, that vehicle could block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or damage.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards for the best protection. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: To reduce collision risk, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To reduce collision risk, always keep a good space cushion around your motorcycle. Maintain this space when following other vehicles, being followed, passing, being passed, or lane sharing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white background with red and black markings. It tells drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Watch what is ahead of you on the road. But also watch what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: You can reduce serious injury in a crash by wearing:
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury when riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield also helps protect your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, they should:

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time to stop quickly. Look ahead on the road to avoid needing sudden stops.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency.
Should be used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: All maintain safe following distances.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps riders together while maintaining safe distances between motorcycles.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster the alcohol is removed from your body.
The faster the alcohol builds up in your body.
The less the alcohol affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster the alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking quickly causes alcohol to build up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will still be in your system after an hour passes.

questions.question: When cars are merging from an entrance ramp:

options.text: A motorcyclist should assume the entering drivers see them.
A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Never assume the drivers see you. Change lanes away from entering traffic if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.
